comparisons.evidence: P's strongest levers, such as the "Circular Provenance Loop" and paid "Reading Prescriptions," improve repeat visits and service margin. Q combines a "Residual-Value Exchange" with an "Outcome & Credential Lab" and a "Demand-Backed Local IP Foundry," addressing transaction economics, institutional revenue, and ownership of non-price-comparable products.

P plausibly links a "buy-back guarantee" to store returns, but its claim that local provenance makes copies "non-substitutable" depends on uncertain willingness to pay. Q gives a tighter reinforcing loop: guaranteed buybacks create returned inventory, used inventory improves margins and price competitiveness, and buybacks generate repeat visits.

P's consumer-paid "$25 reading diagnostic" and "provenance pricing" require unfamiliar willingness to pay, while its publisher-data model raises trust concerns. Q shifts the reading-service payer toward "schools, employers and parents," uses pre-sales for cohorts and IP, and proposes manual pilots before software investment, reducing adoption and capital risk.

P specifies useful pilots such as testing buybacks in two stores and diagnostics for one month. Q more concretely defines the operating changes: quote "30-, 60- and 90-day buyback" values, accept returns at any branch, grade and reroute stock, and presell a six-week outcome cohort with pre- and post-tests.

P offers non-obvious reframings including "Author Equity Stakes," "Slow Ship Arbitrage," and charging directly for curation. Q's credible innovations go further structurally through publisher-held inventory risk, demand-backed creation of exclusive IP, verified reading outcomes, and treating books as assets with visible residual value.

P spans resale liquidity, paid diagnosis, publisher-funded discovery, space rental, coaching, consignment, and royalty participation. Q covers those broad regions while also adding distinct mechanisms for inventory-risk transfer, institutional credentials, pre-funded IP ownership, household-library lifecycle management, distributed book infrastructure, attention contracts, and authenticated collectibles.

P ultimately concentrates on two complementary mechanisms—"Circular Provenance Loop" and "Reading Prescriptions"—but carries speculative detours such as "Slow Ship Arbitrage" and "Author Equity Stakes." Q narrows to two practical recommendations and one wildcard, yet likewise retains weaker diversions such as "Reader Capital Pools," "Civic Memory Nodes," and "Attention Escrow."
